evals.prompt: I just signed up at mubert.com/api, help me set up my credentials
evals.expected_output: The agent asks for company-id and license-token, then asks about single-user vs multi-user usage
assertions: The response asks the user for their company-id and license-token
The response mentions mubert.com/api as the source for credentials
The response asks whether the user needs single-user or multi-user setup

evals.prompt: Set up Mubert API for my personal project. My company-id is abc-123 and license-token is xyz-456
evals.expected_output: The agent validates credentials, creates a customer, and saves everything to .env
assertions: The code validates service credentials by calling GET /service/licenses
The code creates a customer via POST /service/customers
The code extracts customer-id and access-token from the response
The code writes all 4 credentials to .env file
The response mentions that generated music is royalty-free

evals.prompt: I need to set up Mubert for a multi-user app with thousands of users
evals.expected_output: The agent asks for service credentials and then generates a customer provisioning module
assertions: The response asks for company-id and license-token
The code generates a provisioning module/function that creates customers dynamically
The provisioning code calls POST /service/customers with a user identifier

The provisioning code treats POST /service/customers as idempotent (re-posting an existing custom_id returns the same customer and the same access token), or looks an existing customer up with GET /service/customers/custom-id/{custom_id}
The provisioning code sanitises the app's user id into a valid custom_id (^[a-zA-Z0-9._@-]+$, 1-255 characters)
Only MUBERT_COMPANY_ID and MUBERT_LICENSE_TOKEN are saved to .env (not customer credentials)

evals.prompt: Check if my Mubert API is already configured
evals.expected_output: The agent checks environment variables and .env file for existing credentials and validates them
assertions: The code checks for MUBERT_COMPANY_ID, MUBERT_LICENSE_TOKEN, MUBERT_CUSTOMER_ID, MUBERT_ACCESS_TOKEN
The code checks .env file in the project root
If found, the code validates by calling the Mubert API
The response clearly states whether credentials are valid or not

evals.prompt: My Mubert credentials aren't working, can you help?
evals.expected_output: The agent validates the existing credentials and reports which ones are invalid
assertions: The code reads existing credentials from environment or .env
The code validates service credentials via GET /service/licenses
The code validates customer credentials via GET /public/playlists
The response clearly indicates which credentials failed and suggests re-checking at mubert.com/api

evals.prompt: Save my Mubert API key to .env
evals.expected_output: The agent asks for the credentials and saves them to .env with proper formatting
assertions: The response asks which credentials the user wants to save
The code writes credentials to .env file
The .env format includes comments explaining each variable
The response mentions checking .gitignore for .env
